role.altitude: The week is still on the unit: counting who is present, watching, searching, and writing what happened. Less of it is hunting a housing line, a rule card, a search list, or retyping a charge already on the booking line.
reach: The records clerk posts the housing line before the head count.
The shift supervisor posts the rule card for the housing activity.
The shift supervisor posts the search list of cells and vehicles.
The booking officer posts the booking line before the daily log.
skills_to_grow: Refuse a camera match in place of a count
Refuse a conduct score in place of watching

role.ambitious_version: The housing line, the rule card, the search list and the booking line are already posted. The officer still counts, watches, searches, and writes the sentence.

tasks.short: Conduct head counts so each prisoner is present

steps.what: Read the posted housing line before the head count.
Conduct head counts so each prisoner is present.

tasks.design: The count stays the officer walking the unit and seeing who is present. The read in {DOCS} is shorter because the records clerk already posted unit id, prisoner id, name and expected status, so the officer reads one line. Nothing matches a face, sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: The expected names lived in a paper book or in scraps, so the officer rebuilt the line before the count that was the work.
tasks.enabler_now: The records clerk's housing line in {DOCS} is one unit, the prisoner id, the name and the expected status.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing who is actually present, and calling a count short, stays with the officer on the unit.
tasks.human_edge: The officer can refuse a posted line that does not match the people in front of them.
tasks.altitude: The count stays the same length. The shorter piece is finding the housing line.

reach.task: Post the housing line before the count
reach.learn: The officer reads one line and does not rebuild it from the paper book.

reach.task: Hear that the count was done
reach.learn: The count is still the officer's. The line does not replace it.

evidence.claim: Article 5(1)(h) requires prior authorisation for real-time remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces. This count is the officer looking. It is not a biometric match, and the article is not used as a ban on cameras inside a wing.
Calling the count short is the officer's own judgement. This design adds no presence score.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one housing unit, one shift, one correctional officer. They count who is present. They do not book prisoners in, sentence them, or decide sanctions. The documents prior of 6 and the screen prior of 2 are the housing-line read, share 8. The in-person prior of 91, plus the sheet prior of 0.6 and the mail prior of 0.4, is the count, share 92. Those scraps sit inside the count and are not a separate saving. No separate admin task is added.

Housing-line contract, produced by the records clerk before the count, outside this task: unit id, prisoner id, name, expected status (on unit, court, work, hospital). No risk score. The officer reads that line in {DOCS}, which is why the read drops to 75 percent; they still read it. If the line is blank they use the paper book and the read is not shorter. The clerk's posting time is the clerk's, not the officer's. Capture sits in the read. There is no machine step, no send, no alert, no sheet fill, and no step at zero remaining time.
The count itself is unchanged, so that step stays at 100 percent. Upkeep of 0.2 hours per 100 is rechecking a stale housing line. The store running is not the officer's time.
unknowns: Whether this institution's records clerk posts unit id, prisoner id, name and expected status before the count.
How often that line is blank, so the officer still uses the paper book.
research_questions: How often is the housing line blank at the start of the count?
How often does the posted expected status differ from who is on the unit?

already_counted.description: Reading the housing line once it is open.

incremental.description: Recheck a stale housing line before the count. The walk stays on the unit.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A count where the housing line is blank and the officer uses the paper book lands near 0. A count where the line is posted and the officer only reads it, then walks the unit, lands near 1.2. The count itself stays full length.

tasks.short: Monitor conduct and prevent escape or violence

steps.what: Read the posted rule card for this housing activity.
Monitor conduct of prisoners during work or recreational activities.
Act under the procedures to prevent escape or violence.

tasks.design: Watching the activity and stepping in stay full length, because that judgement is the officer's. The read in {DOCS} is shorter because the shift supervisor already posted the unit, the activity and the movement rule. There is no conduct score, no forecast, no send, no alert and no sheet fill.
tasks.previous_blocker: The movement rule lived in a standing order the officer carried from memory, so they rebuilt it before the watch that was the work.
tasks.enabler_now: The shift supervisor's rule card in {DOCS} is one unit, one activity and one movement rule.
tasks.still_hard: Noticing conduct, and deciding to step in, stays with the officer on the unit.
tasks.human_edge: The officer can ignore a posted rule that does not fit the activity in front of them and follow the procedure that does.
tasks.altitude: The watch and the intervention stay the same length. The shorter piece is finding the rule card.

reach.task: Post the rule card for this activity
reach.learn: The officer reads one card and does not reconstruct the movement rule from memory.

reach.task: Take part in the housing, work or recreation activity
reach.learn: The officer still watches and still steps in. The card does not replace that.

evidence.claim: Article 5(1)(d) bans offence prediction solely from profiling. Watching the unit is not a conduct score and not a prediction of who will be violent.
The crime forecast CAS was phased out on 1 December 2025 after an evaluation. This design does not forecast who will be violent.

The in-person prior of 85 is the watch, share 59, and the intervention, share 30. The supervisor's posting time is the supervisor's, not the officer's. Capture sits in the read. There is no machine step, no send, no alert, no sheet fill, and no step at zero remaining time.
Watching and intervening are unchanged, so those steps stay at 100 percent. Upkeep of 0.2 hours per 100 is rechecking a stale rule card. The store running is not the officer's time.

How often that card is missing, so the officer still uses the standing order.

tasks.short: Search prisoners, cells and vehicles for contraband

steps.what: Read the posted search list of cells and vehicles.
Search prisoners for weapons, drugs and other contraband.
Conduct shakedowns of cells for valuables and contraband.
Search the vehicles named on that list.

tasks.design: Searching the person, the cell and the vehicle stays full length. The read in {DOCS} is shorter because the shift supervisor already posted the location and the search type. The list names places, not people ranked by risk. Nothing classifies an object, sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. What was found is written on the daily log, which is a different task.
tasks.previous_blocker: The locations lived in a spoken order, so the officer rebuilt the list before the search that was the work.
tasks.enabler_now: The shift supervisor's search list in {DOCS} is a location id and a search type: prisoner, cell or vehicle.
tasks.still_hard: Searching the person, the cell and the vehicle, and judging what was found, stays with the officer.
tasks.human_edge: The officer can search a place the list missed, and can refuse a list that ranks people instead of naming places.
tasks.altitude: The three searches stay the same length. The shorter piece is finding the search list.

reach.task: Post the search list of places
reach.learn: The officer reads the places and does not wait to hear them again.

reach.task: Be present for the search of person or cell
reach.learn: The officer still searches. The list does not replace the search.

evidence.claim: Article 5(1)(d) bans offence prediction solely from profiling. The search list is places the supervisor named, not a ranking of people.
The officer searches the person, the cell and the vehicle. Nothing in this design classifies an object as a weapon or a drug.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one housing unit, one shift, one correctional officer. They search the people, cells and vehicles the supervisor named. Those scraps stay inside the searches and are not a separate saving. No separate admin task is added.

The officer reads that list in {DOCS}, which is why the read drops to 75 percent; they still read it. If the list is missing the supervisor names the locations aloud and the read is not shorter. The supervisor's posting time is the supervisor's, not the officer's. Capture sits in the read. There is no machine step, no send, no alert, no sheet fill, and no step at zero remaining time.
The three searches are unchanged, so those steps stay at 100 percent. Upkeep of 0.2 hours per 100 is rechecking a stale search list. The store running is not the officer's time.

How often that list is missing, so the supervisor still names the locations aloud.

tasks.short: Record identification, charges and inmate disturbance

steps.what: See the prisoner during the incident on the unit.
Ask about the inmate disturbance and listen.
Read the custody booking line for prisoner identification and charges.
Confirm prisoner identification and charges on the daily log.
Record information on incidents of inmate disturbance and prisoner activities.

tasks.design: Seeing the incident, asking, and writing the disturbance sentence stay full length. The officer reads the custody booking record, then confirms prisoner id, name and charge code on the daily log in {DOCS}. That confirm is the officer checking those fields against the open booking line, which is shorter than retyping them from the paper warrant. No machine writes the log, sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. The sentence stays the officer's own words.
tasks.previous_blocker: Identification and charges lived on the paper warrant, so the officer retyped them before the sentence that was the work.
tasks.enabler_now: The booking officer's line on the custody booking record is prisoner id, name and charge code, already there when the officer opens the log.
tasks.still_hard: What happened, and the sentence that records it, stays with the officer who was there.
tasks.human_edge: The officer can refuse a booking line that does not match the person in front of them, and can refuse a sentence they did not write.
tasks.altitude: The time on the unit and the disturbance sentence stay the same length. The shorter pieces are finding the booking line and confirming identification and charges.

reach.task: Post the booking line before the log
reach.learn: The officer confirms prisoner id, name and charge code and does not retype them from the warrant.
The sentence is still the officer's. The confirm does not replace it.

evidence.claim: A randomised trial of Draft One in New Hampshire found reports were not written faster. This design does not generate the disturbance sentence.
BEAR tags sentences by topic and orders documents; summarising was rejected because details matter. The officer keeps their own words on the disturbance.
Wpg art. 7a: solely automated decisions with adverse effect need prior human intervention. The daily log does not impose a sanction.
Prisoner identification and charges are criminal-offence data. The confirm records only prisoner id, name and charge code, and the officer checks each field.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one housing unit, one shift, one correctional officer, writing the daily log after an incident they saw. They do not book prisoners in, sentence them, or decide sanctions. The in-person prior of 59.5 is seeing the incident, share 42, and asking, share 18. The documents prior of 25.2, the screen prior of 8.8, the sheet prior of 3.8 and the mail prior of 2.7 are the booking-line read, share 10, the confirm, share 12, and the disturbance sentence, share 18. No separate admin task is added.

Booking-line contract, produced by the booking officer before this log, outside this task: prisoner id, name, charge code. No risk score. The officer reads that line on the custody booking record, which is why the read drops to 75 percent; they still read it. If the line is missing they copy the fields from the paper warrant and the read is not shorter. The booking officer's posting time is theirs, not this officer's. Capture sits in the read.

The confirm is the officer writing prisoner id, name and charge code onto the daily log after checking them against that booking line. It is shorter than retyping the same fields from the paper warrant, which is why it drops to 70 percent, and the officer still checks each field. If the line is missing they type the fields and this step is not shorter. If the shift supervisor has posted an incident-type list, it is a type code only, and looking at it sits inside the sentence step, which stays at 100 percent. There is no machine step, no send, no alert, no sheet fill, and no step at zero remaining time.

Seeing the incident, asking, and writing the disturbance sentence are unchanged, so those steps stay at 100 percent. Upkeep of 0.3 hours per 100 is rechecking a stale booking line. The store running is not the officer's time.
unknowns: Whether this institution's booking officer posts prisoner id, name and charge code before the log.
Whether this institution's works council treats the shorter log confirm as staff monitoring.
research_questions: How often is the booking line missing when the officer writes the log?
How often does the officer reject the posted identification because it does not match the person?

already_counted.description: Reading the booking line once it is open.
Confirming identification and charges on the log.

incremental.description: Recheck a stale booking line before the confirm. The disturbance sentence stays the officer's.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A log where the booking line is missing and the officer types identification and charges from the warrant lands near 0. A log where the line is open and the officer only confirms those fields, while the disturbance sentence stays full length, lands near 3.5. Seeing the incident and asking stay full length.
